job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: Last Tuesday, Mr. Sharma invited our Class 6 students to his workshop in Karol Bagh to learn about wood. The workshop was filled with the smell of sawdust and the sound of buzzing tools. Mr. Sharma explained that wood expands when it absorbs moisture from the humid air, which is why wooden doors often stick during the monsoon season. He showed us 12 different types of chisels kept on a wooden rack. My friend Rohan picked up a heavy mallet, while Meera carefully examined a smooth piece of teak. Mr. Sharma pointed out that the workshop floor was made of concrete to prevent fire hazards. He mentioned that he has been working with wood for 35 years. To demonstrate his point about moisture, he placed a dry block of pine in a bowl of water for 2 hours. By the end of the visit, we understood that wood is a living material that reacts to its environment. We thanked Mr. Sharma and returned to school by 4 PM, feeling like real carpenters.
response.summary: Class 6 students visited Mr. Sharma's workshop to learn how wood behaves. They observed how moisture affects wood and saw various tools used by the carpenter.
